name: Bernie Sanders
role: U.S. senator from Vermont (2007-present); candidate for the Democratic presidential nomination (2016, 2020)
summary: Self-described democratic socialist who favors single-payer health care, tuition-free public college, a higher minimum wage, high taxes on wealth, strong unions and worker ownership, and large public climate investment. He opposes most trade deals, the Iraq war and mass surveillance, backs a two-state solution while pressing to cut arms sales to Israel, and rejects open borders while supporting a path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Wrote and has repeatedly reintroduced the Medicare for All Act, covering every U.S. resident, and calls health care a right.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Called for a $15 living wage in 2015 and introduced bills for $15 (2015, 2017, 2019); in 2023 called for $17.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Says he believes in private companies that invest and grow and rejects government ownership of the means of production, but also rejects 'unfettered capitalism' and backs large public programs.

public-ownership.rationale: His 2019 Green New Deal plan puts new renewable power under public ownership via federal power authorities and public utilities; in 2015 he said government should not own the means of production, and earlier (1970s-80s) he sought broad public ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Calls for the wealthiest and largest corporations to pay more: higher estate tax (65% proposal), capital-gains and corporate rate increases, openness to a 90% top rate.

unions-good.rationale: Says the trade union movement built the middle class and set a goal of doubling union membership.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Plan to break up monopolies and mergers, ban stock buybacks, require federal charters for large firms and put workers on boards.

cut-welfare.rationale: Record and platform expand social programs and tie them to rights; he attacks corporate welfare and cuts to the safety net rather than endorsing dependency arguments.

worker-ownership.rationale: Backed worker cooperatives for decades, and proposed that large firms transfer 20% of ownership to workers and let workers elect 45% of boards; it is partial rather than universal worker ownership.

workplace-democracy.rationale: 2020 plan has workers directly elect 45% of the board of large corporations; in 1987 defined democracy as including democratic control of the workplace.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Introduced a bill in 2019 to expand the estate tax and proposed a 65% top estate rate; criticised billionaire families passing on wealth without reasonable estate tax.

central-planning.rationale: Rejecting state ownership of the means of production is nearby; no stated position on central planning.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Supports auditing the Federal Reserve and putting labor, consumer and community representatives on its boards.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Wants higher rates on top incomes, including a 52% bracket and openness to 90%.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Platform: cancel all student debt for about 45 million Americans.

free-public-college.rationale: Wrote the College for All Act and says every qualified person should be able to attend public college tuition-free.

rent-control.rationale: 2020 housing platform called for national rent control capping increases at 3% or 1.5 times inflation.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Signed on to the Be HEARD Act, which ends mandatory arbitration and pre-employment non-disclosure agreements for harassment claims.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Green New Deal plan limits federal funding to publicly owned drinking-water utilities and favours public and cooperative utilities and broadband.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Plan bans permanent replacement of strikers, gives federal workers the right to strike and bars mandatory anti-union meetings.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Plan repeals Taft-Hartley Section 14(b) to end state 'right to work' laws.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Plan includes majority sign-up, first-contract arbitration and public-sector bargaining rights.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: His signature programs are universal (Medicare for All, tuition-free college for all) rather than targeted at the poorest.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Plan rescinds the 'public charge' rule so immigrants can use basic supports, and college-for-all applies regardless of immigration status.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Proposed $1 trillion infrastructure and $16 trillion climate spending paid for by taxes, but voted against the 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act; mixed on deficit as such.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Voted against the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023, which capped spending.

no-bailouts.rationale: Criticised the Wall Street bailout and 'too big to fail' (introduced a bill to break up big banks); his record on bailouts as a general rule is mixed.

ban-cartels.rationale: Plan to break up monopolies and corrupt mergers; wrote bill to break up too-big-to-fail banks.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Opposes corporate welfare and tax breaks, called the CHIPS Act a corporate-welfare 'blank check' and voted against it.

corporate-influence.rationale: Says Wall Street's lobbying and Super PAC money corrupts the system; wants Citizens United overturned and public funding of elections.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Introduced the Inclusive Prosperity Act, a tax on stock, bond and derivatives trading, and cites a Wall Street speculation tax in funding college.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Opposed European austerity measures and urged the ECB, EC and IMF to back pro-growth policies.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Opposed USMCA until it included strong enforcement mechanisms and called for trade deals to protect labor and the environment.

free-trade.rationale: Opposed NAFTA, PNTR with China, the TPP, the Panama FTA and USMCA, saying they cost U.S. jobs.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: A press characterization and Buy America cosponsorship are nearby; no stated position on tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Proposes large public investment in infrastructure and clean energy but voted against the CHIPS Act subsidies to semiconductor firms.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Plan calls for 100% renewable electricity and transport by 2030 and decarbonisation by 2050, $16 trillion in public investment.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Green New Deal plan would stop building new nuclear plants and impose a moratorium on license renewals.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Plan transforms the energy system away from fossil fuels; he opposed Keystone XL and Dakota Access.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Long supported a carbon tax (2014, 2016) but the 2020 plan relied on public investment and regulation.

limit-population.rationale: At a 2019 CNN climate town hall answered yes to a question about empowering women to curb population growth, framing it as reproductive rights and family planning funding.

future-generations.rationale: Speaks of a moral responsibility to leave the planet healthy and inhabitable for our children and grandchildren.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Says rich countries have a moral responsibility to address international poverty, and his climate plan funds the Green Climate Fund.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Backed California Prop 12 farm-animal welfare law and a ban on new factory farms (CAFOs).

animal-use-humane.rationale: Seeks stronger animal-welfare standards in agriculture rather than an end to animal use.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Says a power structure protects extreme wealth inequality, that billionaires buy elections and that this is an oligarchy.

positive-liberty.rationale: Adopts FDR's view that true freedom requires economic security and says people are not free when they cannot feed their families or get health care.

social-market-economy.rationale: Wants private companies to thrive alongside universal social protection and anti-monopoly rules.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: An early essay argued corporate TV owners sought to numb critical thinking; secondhand summary of an old text.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Supports workplace democracy, with worker-elected boards and cooperatives.

separated-powers.rationale: Led war-powers resolutions asserting that Article 1 gives Congress, not the president, the power to make war.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Calls the political system 'in many respects, corrupt' because of money and lobbying.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Plan would mandate criminal liability for police civil-rights violations, end qualified immunity limits and require investigation of killings in custody.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Wants to cut the prison population by half and reform and demilitarise police, while saying officers deserve respect; does not call for abolition.

empower-police-military.rationale: Seeks to demilitarise police and cut military spending (a 2020 amendment to cut the NDAA failed 23-77).

rehabilitation.rationale: Says to move away from an overly punitive approach and to rehabilitate people who have made mistakes.

death-penalty.rationale: Has opposed the death penalty throughout his career; the plan abolishes it.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Plan abolishes three-strikes laws and mandatory minimum sentences.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Marijuana legalization is nearby; no stated position on legalizing recreational drugs generally.

limit-guns.rationale: Supports banning assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, universal background checks and a buyback, though not general gun prohibition; his earlier record (Brady Act no vote, 2005 PLCAA yes) was more mixed.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted against the Patriot Act and renewals, called the NSA out of control and supports a ban on police facial recognition.

state-harmful.rationale: His platform expands the role of government (single-payer, public college, jobs programs) and says government belongs to all of us.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Adopts FDR's Second Bill of Rights, with guaranteed economic rights including health care, housing and jobs.

taxation-theft.rationale: Argues the wealthy and corporations must pay their fair share to fund public programs.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Cosponsored the Equality Act and campaigns to root out institutional racism.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted against DOMA in 1996 and stated in 2015 that gay Americans in every state should be allowed to marry.

abortion-legal.rationale: Describes his record as 'literally 100 percent pro-choice' and pledged to nominate only Supreme Court justices who defend Roe.

separate-church-state.rationale: An advocacy group's rating is not his stated position.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Plan commits to rooting out institutional racism and addressing racial disparities in wealth, health, housing and justice.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Platform welcomes refugees and a path to citizenship but in 2015 opposed guest-worker programs and was sceptical of H-1B visas; mixed evidence.

open-borders.rationale: Asked in 2015 about open borders: 'No, that's a Koch brothers proposal'; says it would make Americans poorer.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Says racial disparities and institutional racism remain, with five types of violence against Black and brown Americans.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: In the early 1970s called for abolishing all laws against homosexuality.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Cosponsored the Equality Act (2017), which bars discrimination against LGBT people.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Frames his politics as 'American idealism' and rebuilding the country for working families.

nation-first.rationale: Says unilateral action should be a last resort and wants a coalition including NATO partners, Russia and the Arab League, though he puts rebuilding America first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Supported the 1999 NATO bombing of Yugoslavia to prevent genocide in Kosovo; opposed the Iraq invasion and other interventions.

force-without-un.rationale: Opposed a unilateral invasion of Iraq in 2002 but backed Kosovo bombing without UN Security Council approval.

war-builds-character.rationale: Describing the costs of wars is nearby; no stated position on war and national character.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Wants to expand on NATO-style collective defence for the 21st century and backs allies against Russia; also wants troops home from endless wars.

collective-defense.rationale: Praises NATO as 'collective defense against a common enemy' and wants a similar organisation against violent extremism.

arms-reduction.rationale: Voted for New START, cosponsored legislation to prevent a post-INF arms race and sought to cut the Pentagon budget.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Says he will never hesitate to defend the nation and has backed veterans and defence of allies.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Opposed Iraq and 'perpetual war' but supported the Kosovo intervention and the 2001 AUMF.

non-intervention.rationale: Supported intervention in Kosovo to prevent genocide, so does not hold that no state may intervene for any reason.

defeat-communism.rationale: Supported normalising relations with Cuba ('Fifty years of Cold War is enough') and said the U.S. does not want a Cold War with China.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Said Israel has the right to exist (2015) and in 2024 that it had an absolute right to respond to October 7; in 2025 said he is not a Zionist 'within the terms of what Zionism means' and called Gaza a genocide.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Supports a two-state solution and criticised West Bank settlement expansion and village demolitions.

national-self-determination.rationale: Says Palestinians deserve a state of their own and that Ukraine's sovereignty must be supported.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Calling current events genocide is nearby; no stated position on formal recognition of past genocides.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Introduced (with Rep. Casar) the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act in response to perceived extinction-level risk from AI.

notes: Platform pages are archived copies of his 2020 campaign site. Sanders's views on Israel have shifted: he affirmed Israel's right to exist (2015) and supported its response to October 7 (2024), then called Gaza a genocide and said he is not a Zionist (2025). The 1970s-80s public-ownership statements are older than his 2015 'government should not own the means of production' line. Books (Our Revolution, Where We Go from Here, It's OK to Be Angry About Capitalism) could not be obtained as full text and are not cited.
